question_text: A television was purchased for £$2000$, and depreciates at $30\%$ p.a. for $3$ years.

subparts.stem: Find the value of the television at the end of this period.
subparts.solution:
$$u_3 = u_0 \times (1 - d)^3$$
$$= 2000 \times (0.7)^3 \quad \{30\% = 0.3\}$$
$$= 686$$
$$\text{So, after 3 years the value of the television is } \text{£}686.$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Annual depreciation reduces the item's value by multiplying by $(1 - d)$ each year: $u_n = u_0(1 - d)^n$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using simple depreciation $2000 - 3 \times (0.3 \times 2000)$ instead of reducing balance depreciation.

subparts.stem: By how much has the television depreciated?

mark_breakdown.desc: Subtracting remaining value from initial purchase price

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Total depreciation is the difference between initial value and current value: $\text{Depreciation} = u_0 - u_n$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Confusing the total depreciation amount with the remaining value.
